root_cause_summary: The reward function imposes a constant step penalty of -0.020 on every valid applied move. When an operator runs but produces zero cost improvement (delta_J == 0), the resulting reward is exactly -0.020. In contrast, inapplicable operators receive -0.050, moves that worsen cost receive < -0.020, and invalid moves receive -1.000. Because PortfolioHybrid baselines on compact plans are already highly optimized, improving moves are rare. WORST_ROUTE_REBUILD (Op 5) evaluates candidate hub rooms that include the current hub room, guaranteeing was_applied=True and delta_J=0. The PPO policy quickly discovered that selecting Op 5 guarantees -0.020 without risk, dominating the expected return of exploring other operators. This caused policy entropy collapse (2.079 -> 0.059) into a safe no-op strategy.

payoff_matrix.scenario: New Incumbent J (-1.0m cost, global best)

flaws_identified.issue: Step penalty asymmetry for zero-change operators
flaws_identified.description: Operators returning zero-delta solutions are treated as successful applications (-0.02) rather than non-improving/inapplicable attempts (-0.05).

With delta_J / J_scale typically 0.02 - 0.05 and step penalty at -0.02, marginal improvements yield near-zero net rewards (+0.00 to +0.03), providing insufficient gradient signal compared to the risk of negative perturbations.

flaws_identified.issue: Absence of exploration bonus / entropy regularization failure
flaws_identified.description: PPO entropy coefficient (0.01) was insufficient to prevent policy collapse against the steady -0.02 vs -0.05 advantage of Op 5.
